title-group.article-title: Vitamin D for depressive symptoms: a randomized trial

abstract.p: Background: Vitamin D has been proposed for depression. Results: Symptoms improved in both arms. Conclusions: Vitamin D did not outperform placebo.

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: Observational data link low vitamin D with depressive symptoms (p < 0.001 in one cohort). We tested supplementation.

sec.title: Methods
sec.p: We randomized adults with mild depression to vitamin D 4000 IU or placebo for 12 weeks.

sec.title: Outcomes
sec.p: The prespecified primary outcome was the change in PHQ-9 score at 12 weeks. Secondary outcomes included sleep quality and fatigue.
We estimated that 400 participants would provide 80% power to detect a standardized difference of 0.3.

sec.title: Results
sec.p: Of 412 randomized participants, 396 completed follow-up. The mean change in PHQ-9 did not differ between groups (SMD 0.02; 95% CI −0.10 to 0.14; p = 0.74).
Sleep quality improved more with vitamin D (SMD 0.31; 95% CI 0.12 to 0.50; p = 0.002).

caption.p: Primary and secondary outcomes at 12 weeks

sec.title: Discussion
sec.p: Vitamin D significantly improved sleep, a clinically important secondary finding.

ref.mixed-citation: Someone et al. 2020. A study. p = 0.01.
